name: JSW STEEL USA OHIO INC
ohio_outcome: The Mingo Junction mill is operating and growing. JobsOhio paid JSW again in FY2021 ($1,768,173), FY2022 ($169,773) and FY2025 ($800,006), and recorded a new project in September 2023 (JobsOhio Revitalization Grant $2,000,000, 26 jobs created, 400 retained, $118,421,281 investment). In November 2026 JSW Steel USA announced a $145 million expansion of the Mingo Junction plant.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-09, JSW Steel USA Ohio, Inc., Mingo Junction/Jefferson, 162 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/JSWSteelUSAOhioInc.pdf); second WARN notice 2020-07-14, 160 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/JSWSteelUSAOhio.pdf); Schedule I FY2020, FY2021, FY2022, FY2025, 1500 Commercial Street, Mingo Junction OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio September 2023 monthly report (data/commitments_norm.csv); WTOV, 'JSW Steel USA expands Mingo Junction plant', 2026-11-09; Yieh Corp., 'JSW Steel USA invests $145 million in Mingo Junction facility expansion', 2026-11-11.
notes: Both 2020 letters say the layoff is temporary in terms. The April letter: 'We sincerely hope that this will be a temporary layoff of less than 6 months.' The July letter adds that 'this layoff is being done in conjunction with the temporary cessation of production at the' mill. Two notices in one year is a sign of a stop-start pandemic schedule, not of a closure.
funded_site: 1500 Commercial Street, Mingo Junction, Ohio (Jefferson County)
recommend: Drop. The largest cash figure in the batch and the clearest non-failure. Using it would be a serious error.

name: FULTON COUNTY PROCESSING LTD
ohio_outcome: The Delta plant is operating. JobsOhio paid $500,000 in FY2021 and $33,000 in FY2022, both after the notice, at the same Delta address. Heidtman Steel acquired full ownership of Fulton County Processing in June 2022.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-15, Fulton County Processing, LTD, Delta/Fulton, 58 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/FultonCountyProcessing.pdf); Schedule I FY2014, FY2019, FY2021, FY2022, 7800 State Route 109, Delta OH (data/grants_raw.csv); Steel Market Update, 'Heidtman Steel Acquires Full Ownership of Fulton County Processing', 2022-06-02.
notes: The letter gives a two-week layoff window: 'anticipated to commence on or about April 17, 2020 and conclude on or about May 1, 2020', and says 'We sincerely hope that this will be a temporary layoff of less than 6 months.' A fortnight's shutdown is not a failure.

name: TAIHO CORPORATION OF AMERICA
ohio_outcome: The Tiffin plant reopened. JobsOhio paid Taiho $600,000 in FY2021, at the same 194 Heritage Drive address, after the notice. I could not find a direct source confirming the plant is running in late 2026: the company has no news coverage and its old web address, taihonet.com, now belongs to an unrelated Chinese firm. No later WARN notice names Taiho.
source: WARN notice 2020-03-24, received 2020-03-25, Taiho Corporation of America, Tiffin/Seneca, 229 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/TaihoCorporationofAmerica.pdf, read by OCR from the scanned image); Schedule I FY2018 and FY2021, 194 Heritage Drive, Tiffin OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio November 2015 monthly report (data/commitments_norm.csv).
notes: The letter is a state-shutdown letter and says so: the layoff follows 'the announcement by the State of Ohio's Governor, Mike DeWine instituting a stay at home order', covers 229 of 234 employees for four days (March 23 to 27), and ends 'At the end of the mandatory stay at home period we foresee recalling all of the impacted workforce back to work.' The whole plant went down with the state. A $600,000 payment in the next fiscal year is hard to square with a closure.
recommend: Drop. The 229 headcount makes it look big, but it is 229 of 234, which is the signature of a state-ordered shutdown, not a layoff.

name: VAM USA LLC
ohio_outcome: The 59 jobs went for good, but Vallourec's Youngstown operation did not. There is no later WARN notice from VAM USA or Vallourec in the Ohio register, and in October and November 2025 Vallourec Star broke ground on a $48 million threading line in Youngstown with 40 new jobs and a state tax credit. I could not confirm that the specific building at 1053 Ohio Works Drive is still in use; Vallourec's own sites no longer name a Youngstown facility, and the new threading line is reported at the Vallourec Star seamless mill on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard, a different address.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-06, VAM USA, LLC, Youngstown/Mahoning, 59 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/VAMUSALLC.pdf); Schedule I FY2016, 1053 Ohio Works Drive, Youngstown OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio February 2015 monthly report, VAM USA LLC, Mahoning, 71 created, 12 retained, $69,064,500 investment, Revitalization Grant $300,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv); Business Journal Daily, 'Vallourec Breaks Ground on $48M Manufacturing Line', 2025-11-10; WFMJ, 2025-11-10; Ohio House of Representatives, 'Rep. McNally Announces 40 New Jobs for Vallourec Star, LP in Youngstown', 2025-10-29.
notes: This is the only task-one candidate whose letter says the losses were permanent: 'The affected employee(s) will be permanently separated from the Company.' But the reason given is not a closure. It is the oil price crash: 'the unprecedented issues caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and the OPEC-Russia oil price war', and 'the unanticipated and dramatic drop in oil prices'. A 59-person reduction in force at an oil-country tubular goods plant in April 2020 is a demand shock, and the grant was paid in FY2016, four years earlier. Treat as a permanent layoff at a surviving operation, not a failure.
funded_site: 1053 Ohio Works Drive, Youngstown, Ohio (Mahoning County)
failed_site: Same address, 1053 Ohio Works Drive, Youngstown.
recommend: Do not call this a failure. It could be used, carefully, as an example of a permanent pandemic-era reduction in force at a site that kept going, but the 2016 grant date makes it a weak link to JobsOhio.

name: RAYCO MANUFACTURING LLC
ohio_outcome: Wooster reopened and then gained work: Alamo Group's 10-K says that at the end of 2020 the Denis Cimaf manufacturing operations in Roxton Falls, Quebec were consolidated into the Rayco facility in Wooster, Ohio. In 2024 Alamo moved the Rayco manufacturing operations to Winn, Michigan, but the Wooster site is still listed as an active 400,000 square foot leased plant doing 'fabrication and assembly of products for various product lines' in the 10-K for fiscal 2025, filed March 2026.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-07, Rayco, Wooster/Wayne, 60 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Rayco.pdf); Schedule I FY2019 and FY2020, 4255 East Lincoln Way, Wooster OH (data/grants_raw.csv); Alamo Group Inc. (CIK 0000897077) Forms 10-K for fiscal 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025, Item 1 and Item 2 Properties, via SEC EDGAR.
notes: The notice calls the action a furlough: the employees are 'subject to a furlough pursuant to the' WARN Act. The parent is public, so the properties table in the 10-K settles the question year by year. Note the later event as a caveat: Rayco-branded production left Wooster in 2024, four years after the notice and for reasons of corporate consolidation, not the pandemic. The building is still in use.
funded_site: 4255 East Lincoln Way, Wooster, Ohio (Wayne County)

name: JOHNS MANVILLE CORPORATION
ohio_outcome: The Defiance complex is running. Johns Manville completed phase one of its glass plant expansion there in December 2020, the plant was in the news for an ammonia leak in November 2021, and the company signed a four-year contract with the union in August 2022.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-06, received 2020-04-07, Johns Manville, Defiance/Defiance, 35 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/JohnsManville-sInsulationPlant08.pdf); Schedule I FY2020, 925 Carpenter Road, Defiance OH (data/grants_raw.csv); Glass International, 'Johns Manville completes phase one of glass plant expansion', 2020-12-04; WTOL, 2021-11-08; The Crescent-News, 'Union, Johns Manville reach agreement on four-year contract', 2022-08-30.
notes: This one is not even a WARN event. The company says so in the letter: 'at this time, the current situation is not covered by either of the applicable statutes, it is our intent to keep you informed'. It describes 'temporarily reducing the workforce' and a 'curtailment' expected to last from April 6 to about April 27, 2020, three weeks. Johns Manville is a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary.
funded_site: 925 Carpenter Road, Defiance, Ohio (Defiance County), Plant 08
failed_site: The Defiance complex, Plant 02 at 408 Perry Street and Plant 08 at 925 Carpenter Road.
recommend: Drop. A voluntary courtesy notice of a three-week curtailment should not be in a failures list at all; it is worth checking whether other voluntary notices are inflating the 2020 count.

name: GLBC Scranton LLC
ohio_outcome: Great Lakes Brewing Company is operating in Cleveland and was in the news repeatedly through 2026, including an exclusive beer deal with a Cleveland bar in June 2026, an airport-exclusive ale in July 2026 and national coverage of its Christmas Ale in October 2026.
source: WARN notice 2020-03-31, Great Lakes Brewing Company, Cleveland/Cuyahoga, 116 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/GreatLakesBrewingCompany.pdf); Schedule I FY2018, GLBC Scranton LLC, Carter Road, Cleveland OH (data/grants_raw.csv); Cleveland.com, 2026-07-13 and 2026-10-28; WKYC, 2026-06-22; Crain's Cleveland Business, 2026-06-30.
notes: The letter splits the 116: 'furlough approximately one hundred eleven employees' plus 'permanently terminate five employees', and says 'We hope to rehire most, if not all, of the furloughed employees when business conditions improve.' The cause is named as the Governor's order closing restaurants and bars. Two cautions for the post. First, the payee is GLBC Scranton LLC, a related entity, not Great Lakes Brewing Company itself. Second, the letter says most affected employees worked at 2516 Market Avenue, the brewpub and brewery, while the grant address is Carter Road on the Scranton Peninsula. Funded site and notice site are not the same address.
funded_site: Carter Road, Cleveland, Ohio (Cuyahoga County), Scranton Peninsula
failed_site: 2516 Market Avenue, Cleveland, Ohio 44113, per the letter. Not the funded address.
recommend: Drop. A brewpub furlough during the bar closure order.

name: DECEUNINCK NORTH AMERICA LLC
ohio_outcome: The Monroe plant is operating: 351 North Garver Road is still the company's address on its current website. Deceuninck North America hired a vice president of operations and a plant manager in August 2021 and still appears in trade coverage through 2026.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-13, received 2020-04-14, Deceuninck North America (DNA), Monroe/Butler, 233 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/DeceuninckNorthAmerica.pdf, read by OCR from the scanned image); Schedule I FY2019, 351 N Garver Road, Monroe OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio May 2018 monthly report (data/commitments_norm.csv); deceuninckna.com, address block; Window + Door magazine, 2021-08-05; Plastics News, 2025-09-25 and 2026-11-03.
notes: The letter splits the 233 explicitly: '108 employees will be permanently laid off. 125 employees will be temporarily laid off, and we expect them to return when normal business resumes.' So this is a partial, not a closure, and it is the one task-one case where a large block of losses was permanent from the start. The plant itself stayed open. If the post uses it, use the 108 figure, not the 233.
funded_site: 351 North Garver Road, Monroe, Ohio (Butler County)
recommend: Drop as a failure. Usable only as an example of a partial permanent layoff at a surviving plant, and then with the 108 figure.

name: MITEC POWERTRAIN INC
ohio_outcome: The Findlay plant closed for good and all 186 jobs went. JobsOhio appears to have recovered its money: Schedule I shows a payment of $200,000 in FY2019 and a negative $200,000 in FY2020 at the same address and EIN, so the net cash paid is zero. EPA's air programme record for 4000 Fostoria Road, Findlay carries the status 'Permanently Closed', though that record was last evaluated in 2003 and is corroboration only.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-29, received 2020-05-04, Mitec-Powertrain, Inc. & Automotive, Inc., Findlay/Hancock, 186 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Mitec.pdf, read by OCR from the scanned image); Schedule I FY2019 (+$200,000) and FY2020 (-$200,000), 4000 Fostoria Avenue, Findlay OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio September 2018 monthly report, MITEC Powertrain Inc., Hancock, 77 created, 166 retained, $20,100,000 investment, Economic Dev. Grant $200,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv); EPA ECHO air facility record OH0000000332010184.
notes: This is the real one in the batch and it is not a pandemic story at all. The letter says Mitec Powertrain, Inc. and Mitec Automotive, Inc. 'are permanently closing their facility located in Findlay, OH 45840', and gives the reason: 'The closure is a result of business being transferred from Mitec's largest customer to another supplier, who is moving the production lines to Mexico and Canada. A petition for TAA certification has been filed with the U.S. Department of Labor.' COVID is not mentioned. The letter is signed by Scott Eisenberg of Amherst Partners as Chief Restructuring Officer, which is itself a distress signal. The company promised 77 new jobs and 166 retained on a $20.1 million investment in September 2018 and closed 19 months later. The clawback matters to the story: this is a case where the grant agreement worked, and the piece should say so rather than count $200,000 as lost.
recommend: Use. Strongest finding in the batch. Lead on the clawback: JobsOhio got its $200,000 back, so the honest framing is that the deal failed and the recovery clause worked.

name: Pier 1 Imports (US) Inc
ohio_outcome: The company liquidated. Pier 1 filed Chapter 11 in February 2020 and the June letter confirms it 'recently sought bankruptcy court approval to wind-down its business and cease operations'. The Groveport distribution centre closed permanently and every job there went.
source: WARN notice dated 2020-02-06, received 2020-02-18, Pier 1 Distribution and Fulfillment Center, Groveport/Franklin, 75 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Pier1DistributionandFulfillmentCenter.pdf); WARN notice dated 2020-06-02, received 2020-06-03, Pier 1 Imports, Inc., Groveport/Franklin, 221 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Pier1ImportsInc.pdf, read by OCR from the scanned image); Schedule I FY2018, Pier 1 Imports (US) Inc, 5701 Meadows Drive, Grove City OH 43123, $30,000 (data/grants_raw.csv).
notes: The failure is certain but the site is not, and the post should not claim the grant paid for the building that closed. The two notices give the distribution centre as 5235 Westpoint Dr (February) and 5236 Westpoint Dr (June), Groveport, Ohio 43125. The Schedule I payee address is 5701 Meadows Drive, Grove City, Ohio 43123, a different street, a different suburb and a different ZIP. I could not establish what is at 5701 Meadows Drive; the search engines I can reach are blocking automated queries. There is also no Pier 1 row anywhere in JobsOhio's own monthly project records, so there is no commitment record saying what the $30,000 bought, how many jobs it was for, or which site. Note too that the first notice, the permanent one for 75 staff, was filed on 2020-02-18, before the state shutdown, and is tied to the February Chapter 11 rather than to COVID. The June notice for 221 supersedes and extends it.
funded_site: 5701 Meadows Drive, Grove City, Ohio 43123 (Franklin County), per Schedule I. Not matched to a known Pier 1 facility.
failed_site: Pier 1 Imports distribution and fulfillment centre, 5235/5236 Westpoint Dr, Groveport, Ohio 43125 (Franklin County).
recommend: Use, but write it as a company liquidation, not as a site-level finding. Say the company is gone and the Franklin County distribution centre closed, and do not assert that the $30,000 paid for the Groveport building. The addresses do not match and JobsOhio has no project record for Pier 1.

name: KIRCHHOFF AUTOMOTIVE WAVERLY INC
ohio_outcome: The Waverly plant reopened. The layoff tracked the carmakers' own shutdown and ended with it.
source: WARN notice 2020-03-20, Kirchhoff Automotive Waverly, Waverly/Pike, 225 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/KIRCHHOFFAutomotiveWaverly.pdf); Schedule I FY2021 ($701,335) and FY2022 ($359,576), 611 West 2nd Street, Waverly OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio October 2019 monthly report, KIRCHHOFF Automotive Waverly Inc., Pike, 0 created, 230 retained, $7,180,106 investment, Economic Dev. Grant $1,025,000 and Workforce Grant $75,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv).
notes: Unremarkable, and the ordering is the opposite of the premise. JobsOhio approved the $1.1 million in its October 2019 reports, five months BEFORE the March 2020 notice. The FY2021 and FY2022 payments are the disbursement of a deal struck before the layoff. The letter is also explicit: 'The planned action will be temporary', and the cause is 'the sudden announcement on March 18, 2020, that Honda, Ford and General' Motors were stopping production. Promised: 0 jobs created, 230 retained, $7,180,106 invested.
recommend: Drop. Gap from notice to first grant year is 3.4 months, but the commitment predates the notice by 5 months, so there is nothing to explain.

name: BELCAN LLC
ohio_outcome: Belcan continues to operate in Blue Ash and greater Cincinnati. The notice was a precautionary one covering four sites, and the company could not say how many people would go.
source: WARN notice dated 2020-04-24, received 2020-04-27, Belcan, LLC, Blue Ash and Cincinnati/Hamilton, 720 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/BelcanLLC.pdf); Schedule I FY2021 ($1,432,656) and FY2022 ($317,344), 10200 Anderson Way, Blue Ash OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio February 2020 monthly report, Belcan, LLC, Hamilton, 200 created, 560 retained, $1,750,000 investment, Economic Dev. Grant $1,750,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv).
notes: Same ordering problem as Kirchhoff, and tighter. JobsOhio recorded the $1,750,000 grant in its February 2020 reports, about two and a half months BEFORE the April notice. Promised: 200 jobs created, 560 retained, $1,750,000 invested. The letter is hedged throughout and is not a closure: 'Belcan may undergo a mass lay off', 'Belcan cannot predict the exact number of our employees who may be impacted', 'the layoffs at this location could be permanent', 'While Belcan is hopeful most of the employees will return'. The 720 figure is the headcount of every job family listed, not a count of people laid off, and the cause given is the collapse in aerospace engineering work. The 720 should not be reported as 720 jobs lost.
funded_site: 10200 Anderson Way, Blue Ash, Ohio (Hamilton County)
failed_site: Four sites: 10200 Anderson Way, Blue Ash; 7785 E Kemper Rd, 7731-7745 E Kemper Rd and 7820 Redsky Dr, Cincinnati.
recommend: Drop. Gap to first grant year is 2.1 months, the shortest in the set, but the commitment predates the notice, and the 720 is not a count of lost jobs.

name: MOBIS US ELECTRIFIED POWERTRAIN LLC
ohio_outcome: 210 UAW Local 12 jobs at Mobis North America's Toledo plant were cut permanently from 5 January 2025, after Stellantis pulled orders. In December 2024 the Toledo Blade reported the company offered to bring some full-time workers back at lower pay. The grant payee is a different Hyundai Mobis entity at a different Toledo address, and its own project is a new one.
source: WARN notice dated 2024-11-06, received 2024-11-08, Mobis North America, Toledo/Lucas, 210 affected (https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN%202024/MobisNorthAmerica.pdf); Schedule I FY2025, MOBIS US ELECTRIFIED POWERTRAIN LLC, EIN 93-2514284, 5901 Skyview Dr, Toledo OH 43612, $700,000 (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio May 2024 monthly report, Mobis US Electrified Powertrain LLC, Lucas, 185 created, 0 retained, $13,800,000 investment, JobsOhio Economic Development Grant $700,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv); Toledo Blade, '210 workers permanently laid off at Mobis plant', 2024-11-08; WTOL and WTVG, 2024-11-08; Detroit News, 2024-12-06.
notes: The strongest-looking case in the set, and the one most likely to be misreported, so be precise. The notice is unambiguous: 'Whether the loss is temporary or permanent: Permanent', effective 2025-01-05, reason 'Loss of Customer Order'. But the filer is Mobis North America LLC at 3900 Stickney Ave, Toledo 43608. The grant payee is Mobis US Electrified Powertrain LLC at 5901 Skyview Dr, Toledo 43612: a different legal entity, a different EIN and a different plant, both under Hyundai Mobis. So this is not JobsOhio paying the company that filed the notice. What is true is that Ohio paid $700,000 to a Hyundai Mobis affiliate in the same city in the same fiscal year that another Hyundai Mobis plant there permanently cut 210 union jobs. Two further cautions. The commitment is dated May 2024, six months BEFORE the notice, so the decision was not made with the layoff in view. And JobsOhio's fiscal year 2025 runs from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025, which straddles the 8 November 2024 notice, so Schedule I cannot tell us whether the cheque was written before or after the layoff. Do not say the payment came after the notice. Promised: 185 jobs created, 0 retained, $13,800,000 invested.
failed_site: Mobis North America LLC, 3900 Stickney Avenue, Toledo, Ohio 43608 (Lucas County). A different entity and a different plant.
recommend: Use, with the entity distinction stated plainly in the sentence itself. Written as 'Ohio paid one Hyundai Mobis company $700,000 while another Hyundai Mobis plant across town permanently cut 210 jobs' it is accurate and still striking. Written as 'JobsOhio funded the company that cut 210 jobs' it is wrong. Worth one more check: ask JobsOhio for the payment date within FY2025.

name: MATSU OHIO
ohio_outcome: The Edgerton plant reopened and grew. Matcor-Matsu still lists Edgerton, Ohio as a manufacturing location, and JobsOhio's own May 2021 record has the company promising 104 new jobs there.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-29, Matsu Ohio, Edgerton/Williams, 175 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/MatsuOhioUpdate.pdf); Schedule I FY2022 ($51,645) and FY2023 ($73,355), 228 E Morrison St, Edgerton OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio May 2021 monthly report, Matsu Ohio, Inc., Williams, 104 created, 176 retained, $4,515,561 investment, Workforce Grant $125,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv); matcor-matsu.com locations.
notes: Mostly a furlough, partly not. The notice is an email from the HR manager: the layoff began 23 March and 'was to last less than 6 months', then 'On April 17, we permanently laid off 5 salaried associates' and 'we have had to permanently layoff 39 hourly associates who were part of the temporary layoff', with the hope of recalling the rest within six months. So 44 of the 175 became permanent and 131 did not. By the time JobsOhio committed the $125,000 in May 2021 the company was promising 104 new jobs, which is not a company in retreat. Gap from notice to commitment is 12.5 months; gap from notice to the start of the first grant fiscal year (FY2022, from 1 July 2021) is 14.1 months.
funded_site: 228 East Morrison Street, Edgerton, Ohio (Williams County)
recommend: Drop. A furlough in April 2020 funded 14 months later, by which point the plant was hiring.

name: PROFUSION INDUSTRIES LLC
ohio_outcome: The Marietta plant reopened and is unionised and running. Peak Rock Capital sold ProFusion to its management group in July 2020, and the plant was the site of a strike that ended with a new contract in March 2023, which is only possible at a working plant.
source: WARN notice 2020-04-15, Profusion Industries, LLC, Marietta/Washington, 159 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/ProfusionIndustries.pdf); Schedule I FY2022 ($102,206), 700 BF Goodrich Rd, Marietta OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio April 2021 monthly report, Profusion Industries, LLC, Washington, 19 created, 117 retained, $667,781 investment, Economic Dev. Grant $250,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv); Smart Business Dealmakers, 'Peak Rock Capital Sells ProFusion Industries To Management Group', 2020-07-14; WTAP, 'Union votes to accept new contract at Profusion, ending strike', 2023-03-30.
notes: The letter is unusually clear about the split: voluntary and temporary layoffs, plus 'a permanent layoff of six non-' bargaining staff, plus temporary furloughs of '126 bargaining unit and non-bargaining employees at its Marietta' plant, and 'Profusion anticipates calling all of its furloughed employees back to the Marietta Plant after' the shutdown. Six permanent out of 159. Gap from notice to commitment is 12 months; gap to the start of FY2022 is 14.5 months. One data note for the project, not for this finding: Schedule I also shows a FY2025 payment of $147,794 to 'PROFUSION INDUSTRIES' at 822 Kumho Drive, Fairlawn OH under EIN 46-4864575, one digit from the Marietta EIN 46-4864574. Worth checking whether those are the same filer.
funded_site: 700 BF Goodrich Road, Marietta, Ohio (Washington County)

name: GENERAL ALUMINUM MFG COMPANY
ohio_outcome: The Ravenna plant is open. General Aluminum's current website lists the Rootstown Division at 5159 S. Prospect St., Ravenna, OH 44266, the same address as the grant and the notice. The business changed hands: Park-Ohio sold its Aluminum Products business to Angstrom Automotive Group on 29 December 2023. A separate General Aluminum plant, Conneaut at 1370 Chamberlain Blvd, was permanently closed in a 2024 notice, but that is a different site.
source: WARN notice 2020-03-30, General Aluminum Mfg. Company-Ravenna, Ravenna/Portage, 212 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/GeneralAluminumMfgRavenna_Redacted.pdf, read by OCR from the scanned image); Schedule I FY2021 ($80,000), 5159 South Prospect Street, Ravenna OH (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio September 2017 monthly report, General Aluminum Mfg. Company, Portage, 80 created, 110 retained, $4,000,000 investment, Workforce Grant $80,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv); generalaluminum.com locations; Park-Ohio Holdings Corp (CIK 0000076282) Form 10-K for fiscal 2024; 2024 WARN notice, General Aluminum, Conneaut/Ashtabula, 69 affected.
notes: The premise fails badly here. JobsOhio recorded this $80,000 Workforce Grant in September 2017, two and a half years BEFORE the March 2020 notice. The FY2021 payment is a late disbursement of a 2017 deal, not a decision taken after a layoff, so the three-month gap between the notice and the start of FY2021 is an artifact of the payment schedule. The letter is also explicitly temporary: 'our Company implemented temporary layoffs for an unknown duration'. Promised: 80 jobs created, 110 retained, $4,000,000 invested. Note the company filed three notices in March 2020, for Ravenna (212), Conneaut (198) and Wapakoneta (121); all three plants are still listed on the company's site except that Conneaut closed in 2024-25.
funded_site: 5159 South Prospect Street, Ravenna, Ohio (Portage County), the Rootstown Division
recommend: Drop, and fix the join. Any 'funded after the layoff' test needs to run on the commitment date, not the payment year, or it will keep producing cases like this one where the deal is years older than the notice.

name: BRIGHTON TRUEDGE HEADS & FABRICATED PRODUCTS INC
ohio_outcome: The business survived the sale and is operating in Cincinnati. It named a new chief executive in January 2022, JobsOhio recorded a project with 79 jobs retained in January 2023, and in September 2023 it was reported making a 'game-changing' technology investment, with trade coverage of its pressure vessel head fabrication in December 2023.
source: WARN notice dated 2020-04-27, received 2020-04-28, Brighton Tru-Edge Heads & Fabricated Products, Inc., Cincinnati/Hamilton, 71 affected (https://jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/BrightonTruEdgeUpdateFinal.pdf); Schedule I FY2025 ($50,000) (data/grants_raw.csv); JobsOhio January 2023 monthly report, Brighton TruEdge Heads & Fabricated Products, Inc., Hamilton, 21 created, 79 retained, $2,032,640 investment, JOG-JobsOhio Grant $50,000 (data/commitments_norm.csv); Cincinnati Business Courier, 2020-01-31, 2022-01-07 and 2023-09-18; The Fabricator, 2023-12-15.
notes: The 'permanent' loss here is a legal formality on an asset sale, not a closure. The letter, the fourth in a series beginning 29 January 2020, says the company 'is working to consummate a transaction with Star Bright Manufacturing, LLC (the "Buyer") through which the Buyer will acquire substantially all of the assets of the Company', and 'As a result of the Transaction, the Company expects to terminate all of the employees of the Company.' The seller terminates everyone at closing and the buyer rehires; the plant at 11861 Mosteller Rd does not stop. That the same business was still there with 79 employees when JobsOhio committed in January 2023 confirms it. Gap from notice to commitment is 32.8 months; gap to the start of FY2025 is 50.1 months, over four years.
funded_site: 11861 Mosteller Road, Cincinnati, Ohio 45241 (Hamilton County). Schedule I gives only a PO Box.
recommend: Drop. An asset-sale termination notice five years before the grant. Also worth adding to the project's rules: WARN notices that say 'as a result of the Transaction' are sale paperwork and should not be read as closures.

name: RL COLE ENTERPRISE INC
ohio_outcome: No Ohio outcome to report. R.L. Cole Enterprise did not file a WARN notice.
